findings.summary: JSDoc comments restate what the method name already says, adding no information
evidence: /** Lists all rulesets for a repository. */ async list()
/** Gets a single ruleset by ID. */ async get()
/** Creates a new ruleset. */ async create()
/** Updates an existing ruleset. */ async update()
/** Deletes a ruleset. */ async delete()
/** Creates a new label. */ async create()
/** Deletes a label. */ async delete()
/** Extract hostname from a git URL. */ function extractHostFromUrl()
/** Delete a branch ref on the remote via GraphQL deleteRef mutation. */ private async deleteRemoteRef()
/** Create a branch ref on the remote via GraphQL createRef mutation. */ private async createRemoteRef()
findings.suggestion: Remove JSDoc comments that merely restate the method name. Keep comments only when they add context (e.g. error semantics, side effects, non-obvious behavior).

findings.summary: JSDoc @param tags restate parameter names without adding useful information beyond what types provide
evidence: escapeShellArg: @param arg - The string to escape / @returns The escaped string wrapped in single quotes
getCommitStrategy: @param repoInfo - Repository information / @param executor - Optional command executor for shell commands / @param hasAppCredentials - Whether GitHub App credentials are configured
interpolateEnvVars: @param json - The JSON object to process / @param options - Interpolation options (default: strict mode) / @returns A new object with interpolated values
isPermanentError: @param error The error to classify / @param patterns Custom patterns to use / @returns true if the error is permanent
findings.suggestion: Remove @param/@returns tags that just restate the parameter name and type. Keep only when adding non-obvious constraints or semantics.

findings.summary: The pattern `token ? { GH_TOKEN: token } : undefined` is repeated verbatim in multiple files instead of using the centralized buildTokenEnv
evidence: graphql-commit-strategy.ts:271: const tokenEnv = token ? { GH_TOKEN: token } : undefined;
graphql-commit-strategy.ts:444: const tokenEnv = token ? { GH_TOKEN: token } : undefined;
gh-api-utils.ts:37: return token ? { GH_TOKEN: token } : undefined; (this IS buildTokenEnv)
findings.suggestion: Import and use buildTokenEnv from gh-api-utils.ts in graphql-commit-strategy.ts instead of inlining the same logic.

findings.summary: Class-level JSDoc comments restate the class name and add only boilerplate
evidence: /** GitHub Ruleset Strategy for managing repository rulesets via GitHub REST API. Uses `gh api` CLI for authentication and API calls. */
/** GitHub Labels Strategy for managing repository labels via GitHub REST API. Uses `gh api` CLI for authentication and API calls. Note: Uses ICommandExecutor... */
/** GitHub Repository Settings Strategy. Manages repository settings via GitHub REST API using `gh api` CLI. Note: Uses exec via ICommandExecutor... */
findings.suggestion: Remove class-level JSDoc that restates the class name. The 'Note:' about ICommandExecutor usage is internal implementation detail obvious from the code.

findings.summary: GitHub strategies pass tokens via GH_TOKEN env var while Azure/GitLab strategies rely entirely on CLI-level auth with no token parameter
evidence: PRStrategyOptions.token comment: '/** GitHub App installation token (GitHub-only; ignored by GitLab/Azure strategies which use their own CLI auth) */'
AzurePRStrategy destructures but ignores token: const { repoInfo, branchName, baseBranch, workDir, retries = 3 } = options; (no token)
GitLabPRStrategy also omits token from destructuring in all methods
findings.suggestion: This is actually a design choice documented in the types, not an inconsistency. The token field is explicitly documented as GitHub-only. However, the interface carries a field that two of three implementations silently ignore. Consider using discriminated options types or at minimum documenting why in the Azure/GitLab strategy constructors.

findings.summary: All three platform strategies consistently use assert*Repo guards at method entry, providing uniform trust boundary validation
evidence: assertGitHubRepo(repoInfo, 'GitHub PR strategy') in every GitHubPRStrategy method
assertAzureDevOpsRepo(repoInfo, 'Azure PR strategy') in every AzurePRStrategy method
assertGitLabRepo(repoInfo, 'GitLab PR strategy') in every GitLabPRStrategy method
assertGitHubRepo used in all settings strategy methods (rulesets, labels, repo-settings)
findings.suggestion: No change needed. This is a strength. The assert pattern is applied uniformly across all platform-specific code paths.

findings.summary: Token resolution for GitHub App credentials is centralized in resolveGitHubToken, used by both sync and settings paths
evidence: resolveGitHubToken in gh-api-utils.ts: 'Both sync and settings paths use this function'
AuthOptionsBuilder.resolve() calls resolveGitHubToken
sync-command.ts passes pre-resolved token to settings processors
findings.suggestion: No change needed. Token resolution is properly centralized.
